question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

10, 41, 165, 661, ? , 10581, 42325
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2645.

GIVEN

• 10, 41, 165, 661, ? , 10581, 42325

SOLUTION

• Each term follows the rule: (previous term × 4) + 1.

• 10×4+1 = 41; 41×4+1 = 165; 165×4+1 = 661.

• Missing term = 661×4+1 = 2644+1 = 2645.

• Check: 2645×4+1 = 10581; 10581×4+1 = 42325. ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Spot the near ×4 jump (661→2645→10581). Rule is ×4 then +1 — just do 661×4+1.

NOTE

• For rapidly growing series, test ×k+c patterns first: divide consecutive terms to guess k, then find the constant.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

Y, V, Q, N, I, F, A, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. X.

GIVEN

• Y, V, Q, N, I, F, A, ?

SOLUTION

• Positions: Y=25, V=22, Q=17, N=14, I=9, F=6, A=1.

• Gaps alternate −3, −5: 25−3=22, 22−5=17, 17−3=14, 14−5=9, 9−3=6, 6−5=1.

• Next gap is −3: 1−3 = −2 → +26 (wrap) = 24 = X.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Alternating −3/−5 pattern; from A(1) subtract 3 and wrap around the alphabet to get X.

NOTE

• When a backward letter series passes A, continue by adding 26 (Z=A−1). EJOTY helps fix letter positions fast.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(NS, HM, AF)

(RB, LV, EO)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (VJ, PD, IW).

GIVEN

• (NS, HM, AF) and (RB, LV, EO)

SOLUTION

• Within a set, going cluster-1 → cluster-2 both letters shift −6, and cluster-2 → cluster-3 both letters shift −7 (with alphabet wrap).

• Check NS→HM→AF: N−6=H, S−6=M; H−7=A, M−7=F. ✓  RB→LV→EO: R−6=L, B−6=V(wrap), L−7=E, V−7=O. ✓

• Option (VJ, PD, IW): V−6=P, J−6=D; P−7=I, D−7=W(wrap). ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Only the first letters need checking: V→P→I is −6 then −7, matching N→H→A. That alone fixes Option.

NOTE

• In cluster-set questions, both letters of each pair usually move by the same step; verify one column then confirm.

question: What will be the sum of the number of Wednesdays in the months of July and September in the year 2005?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 8.

GIVEN

• Year 2005; count Wednesdays in July and September.

SOLUTION

• 1 Jan 2005 = Saturday. Days to 1 July = 181 → 181 mod 7 = 6 → 1 July = Friday.

• July (31 days): first Wednesday = 6 July → 6,13,20,27 = 4 Wednesdays.

• 1 Sept = Thursday (July+Aug = 62 days after Friday). Sept (30 days): Wed = 7,14,21,28 = 4 Wednesdays.

• Total = 4 + 4 = 8.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• A 31-day month has 5 of only its first 3 weekdays; a 30-day month has 5 of its first 2. Wednesday isn't among those here, so each month gives just 4.

NOTE

• 1 Jan 2005 = Saturday (0 odd days for 2004 complete years). Use odd-day counting for any calendar question.

question: What was the first day of the year 1776?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Monday.

GIVEN

• Find the day on 1 January 1776.

SOLUTION

• Use a known anchor: 1 Jan 1900 = Monday.

• From 1 Jan 1776 to 1 Jan 1900 = 124 years, containing 30 leap years (1800 is not a leap year).

• Odd days = 124 + 30 = 154 → 154 mod 7 = 0 → same weekday.

• Hence 1 Jan 1776 = 1 Jan 1900 = Monday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Count years + leap years between the target and a remembered date; if the total odd days are a multiple of 7, the day is identical.

NOTE

• Odd days = normal years (×1) + leap years (×2), then mod 7. Century years divisible by 400 are leap; others are not.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

581, ? , 693, 749, 805, 861, 917, 973
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 637.

GIVEN

• 581, ? , 693, 749, 805, 861, 917, 973

SOLUTION

• Common difference is constant: 749−693 = 56, 805−749 = 56, 861−805 = 56.

• So missing term = 581 + 56 = 637 (also 693 − 56 = 637). ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Difference between the two known neighbours 693 and 581 spans two steps... simplest: 693 − 56 = 637.

NOTE

• In an arithmetic progression, any missing term = neighbour ± common difference. Find d from any adjacent known pair.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. a square containing a downward triangle with a small square inside it.

GIVEN

• Figure 1 : Figure 2 :: Figure 3 : ?

SOLUTION

• In each analogy pair the outer boundary changes but the inner element (the small shape held by the downward triangle) is replaced.

• Left pair: outer square→outer circle, inner circle stays; the constant is the downward triangle carrying an inner shape.

• Figure 3 is a square with a plain downward triangle; the answer must place a small shape inside that triangle.

• Matching the transformation, the inner shape becomes a small square → Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Keep the outer square of Fig-3 and simply insert the small inner figure — only Option keeps the square outline with a tiny square inside the triangle.

NOTE

• In figure analogies, isolate what is constant (here the downward triangle) and track the single element that changes.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the box with T F (top), C|B (middle), G S (bottom).

GIVEN

• Box1 (A R / M|N / L K) : Box2 (R K / N|M / A L) :: Box3 (G T / B|C / S F) : ?

SOLUTION

• The letters move to fixed new positions. Reading positions (TL, TR, ML, MR, BL, BR):

• New TL = old TR, new TR = old BR, new ML = old MR, new MR = old ML, new BL = old TL, new BR = old BL.

• Apply to Box3 (TL,TR,ML,MR,BL,BR = G,T,B,C,S,F): TL=T, TR=F, ML=C, MR=B, BL=G, BR=S.

• Result = T F / C|B / G S → Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Note the two middle letters simply swap (B|C → C|B) and top-right F drops to bottom-left area — only Option has C|B with G at bottom-left.

NOTE

• For lettered-box analogies, map each corner's destination once from the sample pair, then apply the same map to the third figure.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and fourth letter-number cluster is related to third letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 - Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

ACD10 : EGH100 :: BKL12 : FOP144 :: MPR14 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. QTV196.

GIVEN

• ACD10 : EGH100 :: BKL12 : FOP144 :: MPR14 : ?

SOLUTION

• Each letter shifts +4: A→E, C→G, D→H; B→F, K→O, L→P.

• The number becomes its square: 10→100 (10²), 12→144 (12²).

• For MPR14: M→Q, P→T, R→V and 14→14² = 196 → QTV196.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Letters +4, number squared. 14²=196 instantly rules out the 186 options, leaving QTV196.

NOTE

• Treat the trailing number as a whole (as the note says); common transforms are squaring, ×constant, or ±constant.

question:
Arrange the given words in the sequence in which they occur in the dictionary.

1. Fresh

2. Fret

3. Fresco

4. Frenzy

5. Frequency
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 45312.

GIVEN

• 1. Fresh  2. Fret  3. Fresco  4. Frenzy  5. Frequency

SOLUTION

• All share "Fre"; compare the 4th letter: Frenzy(n) < Frequency(q) < Fres(s) < Fret(t).

• So Frenzy(4) first, then Frequency(5).

• Between the two 'Fres' words compare 5th letter: Fresco(c) < Fresh(h) → Fresco(3) then Fresh(1).

• Finally Fret(2). Order = 4, 5, 3, 1, 2 = 45312.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Only the letters after 'Fre' matter: n < q < s < t, and within 's' words c < h. That gives 4-5-3-1-2 directly.

NOTE

• Dictionary ordering compares letter by letter; move to the next position only when earlier letters are identical.

question: In a certain coded language 'SKIS' is coded as 'UPHP' and 'CHAD' is coded as 'EMZA'. How will 'TURF' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. VZQC.

GIVEN

• SKIS → UPHP, CHAD → EMZA. Find code for TURF.

SOLUTION

• Letter-wise shift pattern is +2, +5, −1, −3.

• Check SKIS: S+2=U, K+5=P, I−1=H, S−3=P → UPHP ✓. CHAD: C+2=E, H+5=M, A−1=Z, D−3=A → EMZA ✓.

• TURF: T+2=V, U+5=Z, R−1=Q, F−3=C → VZQC.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just the first letter T+2 = V already points to Option (only VZQC starts with V).

NOTE

• Derive the per-position shift from a given pair, then apply it position-by-position to the new word.

question: In a certain coded language 'BATES' is coded as 'EESBN' and 'OUSTS' is coded as 'RYRQN'. How will 'TALES' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. WEKBN.

GIVEN

• BATES → EESBN, OUSTS → RYRQN. Find code for TALES.

SOLUTION

• Position-wise shift pattern is +3, +4, −1, −3, −5.

• Check BATES: B+3=E, A+4=E, T−1=S, E−3=B, S−5=N → EESBN ✓. OUSTS: O+3=R, U+4=Y, S−1=R, T−3=Q, S−5=N → RYRQN ✓.

• TALES: T+3=W, A+4=E, L−1=K, E−3=B, S−5=N → WEKBN.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• First two letters T+3=W, A+4=E give 'WE...' — only Option matches.

NOTE

• Fixed positional shifts are the most common SSC coding type; find the constant offsets from one clean example.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

XM53, UH106, RC212, OX424, LS848, HO1696
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. HO1696.

GIVEN

• XM53, UH106, RC212, OX424, LS848, HO1696

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: X, U, R, O, L, ? each −3 → should end at I (X,U,R,O,L,I), but the last term shows H.

• 2nd letters: M, H, C, X, S, ? each −5 → should end at N, but the last term shows O.

• Numbers double correctly: 53,106,212,424,848,1696. ✓

• So the last term should be IN1696; the wrong term is HO1696.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Numbers all double, so the error is in the letters — check the last cluster: I−N expected, H−O given → HO1696 is odd.

NOTE

• In wrong-term series, verify letter progression and number progression separately; the flaw usually sits in one part.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

SUN3, QPG233, OMB465, MIV696, KEP927, IAJ1158
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. QPG233.

GIVEN

• SUN3, QPG233, OMB465, MIV696, KEP927, IAJ1158

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: S,Q,O,M,K,I each −2 ✓.

• 2nd letters should be −4 each: U,Q,M,I,E,A → term 2 needs Q, but shows P.

• 3rd letters should be −6 each: N,H,B,V,P,J → term 2 needs H, but shows G.

• Numbers should increase by 231: 3,234,465,696,927,1158 → term 2 needs 234, but shows 233.

• Every check fails on the 2nd term; correct form is QQH234, so QPG233 is wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The number jumps are 231 (465−234): 3→234 expected but 233 given — QPG233 is the misfit.

NOTE

• Cross-check both letters and the number; when several parts of one term are off by 1, that term is the wrong one.

question: At what time (approximately) (in PM) between 2 PM and 3 PM will the hour and minute hands of the clock be opposite to each other?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2:44.

GIVEN

• Time between 2 PM and 3 PM when the hands point opposite (180° apart).

SOLUTION

• At 2:00 the hour hand is at 60°. Angle gained by minute over hour = 5.5° per minute.

• For opposite hands: 5.5m − 60 = 180 → 5.5m = 240 → m = 43.6 ≈ 44.

• So the hands are opposite at about 2:44 PM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Opposite time = (initial hour gap ± 30) × 60/55 minutes: (60/5.5)+... quick formula gives ≈43.6 → 2:44.

NOTE

• Relative speed of hands = 5.5°/min. Set 5.5m − 30H = 180 (or 0 for coincidence) to locate any hand position.

question: A clock is 5 minutes fast at 10:00 AM and 15 minutes fast at 4:00 PM. At what time (in AM) will it show the correct time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 7:00.

GIVEN

• Clock is +5 min at 10 AM and +15 min at 4 PM.

SOLUTION

• From 10 AM to 4 PM (6 hours) it gains 15 − 5 = 10 minutes → rate = 10/6 min per hour.

• It shows the correct time when it is 0 min fast. At 10 AM it is already 5 min fast, so go back in time.

• Time to shed 5 min at 10/6 per hour = 5 ÷ (10/6) = 3 hours before 10 AM = 7:00 AM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Gains 10 min in 6 hr = 5 min in 3 hr. It was 5 min fast at 10 AM, so 3 hr earlier (7 AM) it was exactly right.

NOTE

• Convert a clock's error to a constant gain/loss rate, then step forward or backward to reach zero error.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the star with a black square at the top and a white diamond at the top-right.

GIVEN

• A four-figure series of an eight-arm star carrying two small shapes (a square and a diamond); the fifth figure is to be found.

SOLUTION

• The two shapes sit on the star's arms. At each step the pair turns clockwise and the square and diamond swap their shading (black ↔ white).

• Continuing this to the fifth figure, the square becomes black and moves to the top arm, while the diamond becomes white and sits on the top-right arm.

• This exactly matches Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Track the top arm: in the ? figure it must carry the black square (with a white diamond beside it) — only Option shows this.

NOTE

• In figure series, follow each element's position and shading as separate cycles; the missing figure must continue both.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. an upright triangle with a median line and 5 dots along the left side.

GIVEN

• Series: upright triangle (1 dot, with line), inverted triangle (2 dots), upright triangle (3 dots, with line), inverted triangle (4 dots), ?

SOLUTION

• Orientation alternates upright / inverted; the upright ones carry a vertical median line.

• The dot count increases by 1 each step: 1, 2, 3, 4, so the fifth figure has 5 dots.

• The fifth position is an upright triangle (following the alternation) with a median line and 5 dots → Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Odd positions = upright triangle + line; the count is just the position number, so #5 = upright with 5 dots (Option).

NOTE

• Handle two rules at once: track orientation (alternating) and quantity (arithmetic) independently, then combine.

question: The present ages of A, B and C are 11 years, 18 years and 21 years respectively. What will be the ratio of ages of A, B and C after 7 years respectively?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 18 : 25 : 28.

GIVEN

• Present ages A = 11, B = 18, C = 21 years.

SOLUTION

• Add 7 years to each: A = 11+7 = 18, B = 18+7 = 25, C = 21+7 = 28.

• Ratio A : B : C = 18 : 25 : 28.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just add 7 to every age; order stays A:B:C, giving 18:25:28 (the middle value 25 rules out the reversed option).

NOTE

• Keep the ratio order identical to the names' order; a common trap is swapping the last two terms.

question: Sum of the present ages of A, B and C is 120 years. 24 years ago from the present the ratio of ages of A, B and C was 5 : 4 : 3. What is the sum of present ages of A and C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 80 years.

GIVEN

• A + B + C (present) = 120; 24 years ago A : B : C = 5 : 4 : 3.

SOLUTION

• Sum 24 years ago = 120 − 3×24 = 120 − 72 = 48.

• Ratio parts = 5+4+3 = 12 → 1 part = 48/12 = 4.

• 24 years ago: A = 20, B = 16, C = 12. Present: A = 44, B = 40, C = 36.

• Sum of present ages of A and C = 44 + 36 = 80 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Past sum = 120 − 72 = 48; A and C were 5+3 = 8 parts = 32, add back 2×24 = 48 → 32+48 = 80.

NOTE

• For 'years ago' problems, subtract (number of people × years) from the present sum to get the past sum before splitting by ratio.
